tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)

   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`

   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

Use the shared [workflow terminology](../../AGENTS.md#workflow-terminology).

# Spec Research & Authoring

Deploy a parallel research team to investigate requirements for a new spec, then synthesize findings into a complete feature specification document. The research phase uses 3 subagents with distinct investigation angles to ensure comprehensive coverage before writing begins.

## Arguments

Accept a spec topic or folder path (e.g., `notifications`, `feature-007`, `docs/notifications/`, or a plain description like "real-time notifications system").  
If a stub README already exists in the feature folder (for example `docs/feature-name/README.md`), read it for initial scope constraints.

## Workflow

### Phase 1: Scope Discovery

Before dispatching researchers:

1. Determine the feature folder name. If the argument is already a folder path, use it. Otherwise derive `docs/spec-NNN-<kebab-slug>/`: read `CLAUDE.md` `## Current State` for the current sequence if present. If `CLAUDE.md` is missing, malformed, or the `## Current State` section is absent, continue with fallback naming logic: list existing `docs/spec-*` folders and use the highest number + 1. If no numbered folders exist, follow whatever folder convention prior specs in `docs/` use; if `docs/` is empty, ask the user to confirm the folder name before proceeding.
2. Read any existing stub (`docs/<folder>/README.md`) for scope constraints.
3. Scan the codebase for existing patterns and integration points.
4. Identify 3 distinct research angles based on what the feature needs to cover.

### Phase 2: Define 3 Research Angles

Select 3 non-overlapping research angles based on the feature domain. Each agent investigates a different facet.

Typical per-domain configurations (infrastructure / domain-feature / security-compliance, always anchored by a Codebase Analyst) are in `references/research-angle-menus.md` — load it when picking the angles.

### Phase 3: Dispatch Research Team in Parallel

Deploy all 3 researchers simultaneously.

- **Codebase Analyst**: use `geeky-orchestration:code-explorer` agent type.
- **Web Researchers (2)**: use `general-purpose` agent type with instructions to use `WebSearch` and `WebFetch`.

Each research brief ends with:

```
Produce a structured report with:
- Key findings (numbered, specific)
- Constraints discovered (what the spec MUST respect)
- Recommendations (what the spec SHOULD include)
- Sources (URLs for web research, file paths for codebase)

DO NOT create or modify any files.
```

### Phase 4: Synthesize into Spec Document

After all 3 researchers report back:

1. Consolidate findings: merge overlap, resolve contradictions, and note confidence gaps.
2. Define scope: goals, non-goals, delegation items.
3. Write the requirements document using the project’s established conventions in:
   - `docs/<feature-folder>/feature-specification.md`
   - `docs/<feature-folder>/README.md`

   Do not create `SPEC-NNNN-*.md` files — that naming is legacy; `feature-specification.md` is the canonical filename consumed by /geeky-plan and the freeze hooks.

   If a stub README already exists, preserve its stated scope and only update the Status line and missing sections; otherwise create the README stub:

   ```markdown
   # [Feature Name]

   [One-paragraph scope summary.]

   **Status:** Spec written — not yet planned
   **Spec:** `feature-specification.md`
   **Next:** /geeky-plan docs/<feature-folder>/
   ```

Use the 11-section recommended spec structure in `references/spec-structure-template.md` (adapt sections to the feature domain; include citations and explicit assumptions at the end of major findings).

### Phase 5: Commit and Suggest Next Steps

Commit the spec (same command on all platforms). The spec is not yet frozen — it only becomes part of the frozen planning contract after /geeky-plan runs:

```
git add docs/<feature-folder>/
git commit -m "docs: author feature specification in <feature-folder>" -m "[1-line summary of the spec focus]" -m "Research conducted by: codebase analyst, researcher 2 domain, researcher 3 domain"
```

Then suggest next steps:
```
Spec written. Next steps:
- /geeky-plan docs/<feature-folder>/   (to create implementation plan, tasks, kanban)
- /plan-review docs/<feature-folder>/  (to validate the planning package)
- /geeky-implement docs/<feature-folder>/ (to execute)
```

## Research Quality Standards

- **Recency**: Target sources from roughly the past 18 months; avoid older sources unless they cover stable fundamentals.
- **Authority**: Prefer official documentation (Microsoft Learn, AWS docs, RFC specs) over blogs or forums.
- **Specificity**: Include concrete findings (resource types, API versions, package versions, pricing tiers).
- **Adversarial verification**: If researchers disagree on a fact, preserve both positions and flag for user decision.

## Rules

- **Always 3 researchers** — one codebase analyst + two web/domain researchers.
- **Parallel dispatch** — all 3 in a single turn for maximum speed.
- **Research before writing** — do not start the spec document until all researchers report back.
- **Cite sources** — every major claim in the spec should trace to research.
- **Respect existing stubs** — if a README stub exists, treat its stated scope as authoritative unless research justifies adjustments.
- **Follow project conventions** — spec format, naming, and folder structure should match prior specs in `docs/`.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 600000ms / 10 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

Build `csvledger`, a small Python command-line tool that reads one or more bank-export CSV files of transactions, assigns each transaction a category using a rules file, and prints a monthly report. It must run as `python -m csvledger` from the repository root using only the Python 3.11+ standard library. Provide two commands: `report` (per-month, per-category totals) and `categorize` (each transaction with its assigned category). Both commands print either an aligned text table or JSON. Money must be exact (no floating point) and output must be byte-for-byte deterministic on Windows, macOS and Linux. Bad input must fail cleanly with a clear message on stderr and a specific exit code, never a traceback. Identical transactions repeated across overlapping exports must be counted once. The full interface contract is in `contract.md`; include pytest tests for your implementation.
------
# csvledger: Interface Contract

## Constraints

- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, standard library only; pytest for tests only.
- **Package location:** `csvledger/` at repo root (flat layout, no `src/`).
- **Entry point:** `python -m csvledger <command> ...` run from repo root.

## Functional requirements

- **R1** `python -m csvledger` exposes subcommands `report` and `categorize`; `--help` exits 0.
- **R2** Transaction files are parsed per the CSV contract; any invalid file or row aborts the run with exit 3 and no stdout.
- **R3** The rules file is parsed per the rules contract; any invalid rule aborts with exit 4 and no stdout.
- **R4** Each transaction gets exactly one category: the highest-priority matching rule; ties go to the rule earliest in the file; no match gives `Uncategorized`.
- **R5** Duplicate transactions (same date, stripped description, and numeric amount value) across all inputs are kept once (first occurrence) and a warning is written to stderr. Deduplication runs over all rows of all input files before the `--month` filter; the warning count N covers duplicates across all inputs regardless of `--month`.
- **R6** `report` aggregates by month and category: count, income, expenses, net.
- **R7** `categorize` lists every transaction, sorted by date ascending, ties in input order.
- **R8** `--month YYYY-MM` restricts both commands to transactions in that month.
- **R9** `--format table|json` selects output; default `table`.
- **R10** Money uses `decimal.Decimal`; sums are exact; displayed values are rounded once to 2 dp, ROUND_HALF_UP, never shown as `-0.00`.
- **R11** Output is deterministic: UTF-8, `\n` line endings, stable ordering, no locale use.

## Interface contract

### Commands

```
python -m csvledger report     [--rules PATH] [--format table|json] [--month YYYY-MM] FILE [FILE ...]
python -m csvledger categorize [--rules PATH] [--format table|json] [--month YYYY-MM] FILE [FILE ...]
```

- `FILE`: one or more transaction CSV paths, processed in argument order. `-` is an ordinary file name; stdin is never read.
- `--rules`: optional. When omitted, every transaction is `Uncategorized`.
- `--month`: must match `^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$`, else usage error.
- argparse `prog` is `csvledger`. stdout is reconfigured to `encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"`.
- Load order: rules file first, then transaction files in argument order. First error wins.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success (including empty result and duplicate warnings) |
| 1 | Reserved for unexpected internal error; never intentional |
| 2 | Usage error (argparse: unknown flag, missing FILE, bad `--format`/`--month`) |
| 3 | Transaction file error |
| 4 | Rules file error |

### Transaction CSV

- Encoding UTF-8, optional BOM (`utf-8-sig`); opened with `newline=""`; parsed with `csv.reader` defaults (comma, `"` quoting).
- Line 1 is the header. Header names are stripped and lowercased; `date`, `description`, `amount` are required, in any order; extra columns are ignored; duplicate names are an error.
- Rows with zero fields (blank lines) are skipped. Every other row must have exactly as many fields as the header.
- `date`: stripped value must match `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` and be a valid calendar date (regex first; do not rely on `date.fromisoformat` alone).
- `amount`: stripped value must match `^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$`. Negative = expense (outflow), positive = income, zero counts but adds to neither.
- `description`: stripped; may be empty.
- A header-only file is valid (zero transactions). A file with no header line (0 bytes) is an error.

### Rules CSV

- Same encoding/header/blank-row/field-count rules. Required columns: `category`, `type`, `pattern`, `priority`.
- `category`: stripped, non-empty. `type`: stripped, exactly `contains` or `regex`. `pattern`: stripped, non-empty. `priority`: stripped, matches `^-?\d+$`.
- `contains`: `pattern.casefold() in description.

   - O1: Groceries is 45.10 + 12.005 = 57.105, which rounds to 57.11 under ROUND_HALF_UP, so the aggregate must be rounded once at display time.

   - O5: Tiny expenses are -0.004, which quantizes to `-0.00` and must print `0.00` (the R10 zero rule).
   - O5: Tiny net is 0.006, which prints `0.01`.
   - O5: Misc has income 0.125, which prints `0.13`.
   - O4: `-4.5` and `-4.50` dedupe because the Decimals compare equal, and the stripped description matches.
8. **Spec gaps and ambiguities** (each needs a decision before coding):
   - What counts as a header when line 1 is blank? `csv.reader` yields `[]` for a blank line, but "no header line" is defined only as a 0-byte file. A BOM-only file also has no header.

   - Which error applies when `int()` raises on a priority of more than 4300 digits? 3.11 limits this conversion. The pattern `^-?\d+$` passes but `int()` raises `ValueError`.

   - What if a quoted description contains a newline? It breaks table alignment. JSON is fine.
   - Tie-break detail: "priority" is an integer, higher wins, and ties go to the earliest rule in the file.

### decimal

1. **`quantize` can fail on large values.** It raises `InvalidOperation` if the quantized coefficient has more digits than the context precision. The default `prec` is 28, so an amount with more than 26 integer digits fails to quantize at 2 places. This is not silent: the default traps include `InvalidOperation`. A context with no traps would return NaN instead.
2. **`ROUND_HALF_UP` means ties go away from zero.** Pass it explicitly: `d.quantize(Decimal('0.01'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)`. The default context rounding is `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, so omitting it is a silent bug. An explicit `rounding=` argument overrides the context.
3. **Negative zero survives quantize.** Signed zero is preserved, so `Decimal('-0.001').quantize(Decimal('0.01'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)` gives `Decimal('-0.00')`. Zeros compare equal regardless of sign, so `== 0` won't catch it. Use `is_zero()` and replace the value with a positive zero (for example `abs(q)`). I'm confident that `format(Decimal('-0.00'), 'f')` prints `'-0.00'` **[unverified in docs]**.
4. **The default `Decimal(str)` constructor is too permissive for a strict parser.** It accepts:
   - surrounding whitespace;
   - underscores such as `1_000`;
   - `Inf`, `Infinity`, `NaN` and `sNaN` in any case;
   - exponents such as `1e5`;
   - non-ASCII Unicode digits, including fullwidth digits.
5. **`Context.create_decimal()` is stricter on whitespace and underscores only.** It forbids both, but it still accepts the other forms above.
6. **`Decimal` stores every digit of a string exactly.** Context precision does not affect construction, so `Decimal('3.00000')` stays as is even at `prec=3`. Arbitrary-length strings are therefore parsed exactly. The C implementation still raises `InvalidOperation` for extreme exponents such as `1e9999999999999999999`.
7. **Addition rounds to context precision.** Summing many long values at `prec=28` silently drops digits and sets the `Rounded` and `Inexact` flags. The fix is one of:
   - set `prec` high enough for the worst case (maximum digits plus about log10(N) carry digits, plus margin) and trap `Inexact` and `Rounded`;
   - sum scaled integers instead.
   The docs' recipe for exact arithmetic is `prec=MAX_PREC, Emax=MAX_EMAX, Emin=MIN_EMIN`. The docs warn that this raises `MemoryError` on 64-bit platforms if a result is inexact (for example, division). It is fine for add-only work, but a bounded `prec` is safer.
8. **`Inexact` is the validator for "more than 2 decimal places".** The docs' FAQ uses `quantize(TWOPLACES, context=Context(traps=[Inexact]))` to reject inputs with excess places. `Rounded` fires even when only zeros are discarded. `Inexact` fires only when non-zero digits are discarded. 9. **`localcontext(prec=..., traps=...)`** supports keyword arguments since 3.11. Python 3.11 is the floor, so the keywords are safe. Use it, or an explicit `Context` object, so that global context state and `getcontext()` thread-locals never affect results.
10. **`format(q, 'f')` is fixed-point and never scientific.** `str()` or `repr()` can produce `1E+2` or `0E-7`. After `quantize(Decimal('0.01'))` the exponent is always -2, so `'f'` gives exactly two places. Note that `format(d, '.2f')` re-rounds using the context's rounding mode (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN` by default). That can silently disagree with the `HALF_UP` result. Always quantize first, then use a bare `'f'`. Avoid the `,` format option.

12. **`utf-8-sig`** strips a leading BOM at decode time, and plain `utf-8` would leave `\ufeff` glued to the first header cell. The csv docs don't mention it, so the BOM handling comes from the `codecs` docs, which I did not fetch **[unverified]**. Combine it with `newline=''`: `open(p, newline='', encoding='utf-8-sig')`.     - Embedded NUL handling is not documented. I recall that NUL is accepted since 3.11, whereas older versions raised `Error` **[unverified]**.
17. **Writer defaults.** The writer's `lineterminator` defaults to `'\r\n'`, and `QUOTE_MINIMAL` is the default quoting. For byte-deterministic output, pass `lineterminator='\n'` (or `'\r\n'` explicitly) and an explicit `quoting`. Open the output with `newline=''` and a fixed `encoding='utf-8'` (no BOM). 18. **`\d` on str patterns matches any Unicode Nd digit**, such as Arabic-Indic and fullwidth digits. `re.ASCII` (or inline `(?a)`) restricts it to `[0-9]`. The alternative is to write the class explicitly as `[0-9]`. That is flag-proof and clearest, but `re.ASCII` is still advisable for `\s` and `\w`.

24. **Verdict for strict ASCII grammars.** For an ASCII-only vocabulary (header names, currency codes, keywords), neither tool is needed. Validate `isascii()` first, then compare exactly or use `.lower()` / `.upper()`. This avoids all of the Unicode surprises above.
25. **Other `str` helpers.**
    - `str.isdigit()` and `str.isdecimal()` both accept non-ASCII digits. `isdigit()` also accepts `²`.
    - `str.isascii()` (3.7+) is true for the empty string.
    - Combine `s.isascii()` with an explicit `[0-9]` regex for digit checks.

- **C1.** Never use `float` anywhere. Parse money only with `Decimal(str)` after a strict regex gate, because the constructor itself accepts underscores, whitespace, NaN/Inf, exponents and non-ASCII digits.

- **C4.** Normalize negative zero after quantizing. The result must be `0.00`, never `-0.00`.

State that it is applied with `fullmatch` on the raw cell. Say whether surrounding whitespace is stripped, and strip it with an explicit ASCII set rather than relying on `str.strip()`'s Unicode default.

  - fullwidth and Arabic-Indic digits;
  - `12\n`;
  - `1_000`;
  - `NaN`/`Inf`;
  - `1e2`;
  - `-0.00` and `-0.004`;
  - a 40-digit amount;
  - an empty file and a header-only file;
  - a BOM;
  - CRLF, LF and bare CR line endings;
  - blank lines;
  - a quoted multiline field.

<result># Research report: stdlib-only `python -m csvledger` (Python 3.11+)

I read the official Python and pytest docs and ran a few quick checks on Python 3.13.15 / Windows 11 (nothing written to disk). The "Verified" items below come from those runs. Anything marked "from general knowledge" is not backed by a fetched doc.

## Key findings

**argparse**
1. **Prog naming.** A subparser's `prog` defaults to the parent prog plus any positionals before the subparser argument. With `ArgumentParser(prog="csvledger")` and `add_parser("report")`, usage shows `usage: csvledger report [-h] ...`.
   - Verified error line: `csvledger report: error: argument --month: invalid month '2024-13' (expected YYYY-MM)`.
   - Without an explicit `prog=`, the name comes from `sys.argv[0]`. Under `-m` that is the module's full file path, so `prog="csvledger"` must be set explicitly.
2. **Error format and exit code.** The default `error()` prints the usage to stderr, then `<prog>: error: <message>`, then exits with code 2.
   - An error raised inside the `report` subparser uses the `csvledger report:` prefix and `report`'s usage.
   - An error raised by the top-level parser (no subcommand, bad subcommand) uses `csvledger:` and the top-level usage.
   - Verified: `csvledger: error: the following arguments are required: cmd` when `dest="cmd"`, and `argument cmd: invalid choice: 'bogus' (choose from 'report')`.
   - The "required" message names the `dest`, so set `metavar` or `dest` deliberately. Python 3.13 prints `cmd` here.
3. **`type=` validators.** If the callable raises `ArgumentTypeError`, `TypeError` or `ValueError`, argparse catches it and exits 2 with `argument --month: <message>`.
   - `ArgumentTypeError` text is shown verbatim. `ValueError` gives the generic `invalid <typename> value: '...'`, using the callable's `__name__`.
   - Any other exception type propagates as a traceback.
   - Validators run only for values actually supplied, not for defaults of non-string type.
4. **Required positionals.** `nargs='+'` with no values gives `the following arguments are required: files`, exit 2. Verified.
5. **`-` as a filename.** A lone `-` is accepted as an ordinary positional string (verified: `files=['-', 'x']`). Treating it as stdin is the program's job. `argparse.FileType` handles it but is deprecated in 3.14 and leaks open files on later errors, so use plain `str` and open the file yourself.
6. **Mixed arguments.** `report -x` printed `required: files` rather than "unrecognized arguments", because the required-argument check fires first. # csvledger Specification

**Status:** Not Started
**Dependencies:** none (greenfield)
**Layer:** Domain (CLI tool)
**Priority:** Critical Path
**Estimated Complexity:** ~12 tasks across 4 phases

**Authority:** `contract.md` at the repo root is authoritative and is not restated in full here. Where this document and `contract.md` differ, `contract.md` wins. This document adds architecture, resolved ambiguities and a test strategy.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

`csvledger` is a stdlib-only Python 3.11+ CLI (`python -m csvledger`) that reads bank-export CSVs, categorizes transactions by a rules file, deduplicates overlapping exports, and prints a monthly report (`report`) or a per-transaction listing (`categorize`) as a table or JSON. Money is exact (`Decimal`), output is byte-deterministic on all platforms, and bad input fails with specific exit codes and no traceback.

## 2. Problem Statement

### Current State
The repo holds only `brief.md`, `contract.md` and a one-line `.gitignore` (`__pycache__/`). No package, tests, config or docs exist. (Source: codebase analyst.)

### Impact of Inaction
No tool; the contract is unmet.

## 3. Goals & Non-Goals

**Goals:** satisfy R1-R11 and AC1-AC10 of `contract.md`; pytest suite covering every row of the error table and every oracle case (O1, O3, O4, O5); byte-exact output on Windows/macOS/Linux.

**Non-goals:** stdin input (`-` is an ordinary filename); locale/currency support; writing CSV; packaging/installation; third-party dependencies; any config beyond `--rules`.

## 4. Architecture

Flat package at repo root (no `src/`):

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `csvledger/__init__.py` | version only |
| `csvledger/__main__.py` | `sys.exit(main())` |
| `csvledger/errors.py` | `LedgerError(message, exit_code)`; `TransactionFileError` (3), `RulesFileError` (4) |
| `csvledger/csvio.py` | shared reader: open `utf-8-sig`, `newline=""`, header checks, blank-row skip, field-count check, `line_num` |
| `csvledger/transactions.py` | `Transaction` dataclass, date/amount validation, dedup |
| `csvledger/rules.py` | `Rule` dataclass, loading/validation, `categorize(description)` |
| `csvledger/report.py` | month/category aggregation |
| `csvledger/render.py` | money formatting, tables, JSON |
| `csvledger/cli.py` | argparse, stream setup, orchestration, error-to-exit-code mapping |

Data flow: parse args → load rules → load each transaction file in argument order (all fully read and validated) → dedup across all rows → `--month` filter → categorize → aggregate/sort → render to a single string → write to stdout, flush → write duplicate warning to stderr. Nothing is written to stdout until all loading has succeeded.

Tests live in `tests/` with `tests/conftest.py`; supporting files: `.gitattributes` (`* text=auto eol=lf`), extended `.gitignore` (`.pytest_cache/`, `*.pyc`, `.venv/`), and a minimal `pytest.ini` (`testpaths = tests`, `pythonpath = .`).

## 5. Detailed Design

Behaviour per `contract.md`. Resolved ambiguities and implementation rules:

1. **Strict ASCII validation.** Use `re.fullmatch` with `[0-9]` (never `^...$` with `match`, never bare `\d`) for date, amount, priority and `--month`. The contract's patterns are read as these ASCII, full-string equivalents. Rationale: `\d` matches Unicode digits; `$` matches before a trailing `\n`; `Decimal()` accepts underscores, NaN and fullwidth digits. (Web research 1, codebase analyst.)
2. **Decimal context.** All arithmetic runs under an explicit local `Context` (`decimal.localcontext`) with ample precision (e.g. `prec=100`) and `Inexact`/`Rounded`/`InvalidOperation` trapped for sums, so sums are exact for any realistic input. Amounts are constructed only from regex-validated strings. Quantize with `rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP` explicitly; never use `format(x, ".2f")`. A very long amount that would still overflow the context is reported as the transaction error `invalid amount` (exit 3) rather than a traceback.
3. **Money formatting** exactly per contract: quantize, map zero to `0.00`, else `format(q, "f")`.
4. **Header handling.** Zero-byte file (or BOM-only) → `missing header`. A first record of zero fields (blank first line) is treated as `missing header`. Header names stripped and lowercased; duplicate/missing checks per contract order.
5. **Reader.** `csv.reader(f)` with defaults per contract. Whole file is read inside the `try` so `UnicodeDecodeError` (not an `OSError`) is mapped to `not valid UTF-8`; `OSError` (including a directory argument, which is `PermissionError` on Windows and `IsADirectoryError` on POSIX) → `cannot read file`. `<line>` is `reader.line_num` after reading the record, per contract. A `csv.Error` (e.g. field larger than the limit) is mapped to `<path>:<line>: expected ... ` is not available, so it is reported as `<path>: cannot read file` (exit 3/4) — an unspecified edge case chosen as the closest contract message.
6. **Priority.** Parsed with `int()` inside a guard; a `ValueError` (e.g. >4300 digits) → `invalid priority '<value>'`. Highest priority wins; ties go to earliest rule in file.
7. **Description** used for matching, dedup, and output is the stripped value. Dedup key: `(date, description, Decimal amount)`; `Decimal` equality makes `-4.5 == -4.50`.
8. **Sorting.** Months and categories sorted by plain code-point string order; `categorize` uses a stable sort by date.
9. **Table.** Cell widths via `len()`; a description containing embedded newlines is output as-is (not escaped); this is an accepted edge case.
10. **CLI.** `prog="csvledger"`; `add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)`; `--month` validated with a `type=` callable raising `argparse.ArgumentTypeError`; `files` positional `nargs="+"` of `str`; `allow_abbrev=False`. stdout is reconfigured to `encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"`; stderr is also reconfigured to UTF-8 (with `errors="backslashreplace"`) so non-ASCII paths cannot raise.
11. **Failure handling.** `main(argv=None) -> int`. `LedgerError` → `csvledger: error: <msg>` on stderr, return its code. A last-resort `except Exception` prints `csvledger: error: internal error` and returns 1. `BrokenPipeError` on output returns 1 silently. argparse `SystemExit(2)` passes through.

## 6. Cost Estimates

N/A (no external services).

## 7. Task Outline (Preliminary)

- **Phase 1 - Foundation:** repo hygiene files; package skeleton; `errors.py`; `csvio.py`.
- **Phase 2 - Domain:** `transactions.py` (+dedup); `rules.py`; `report.py`.
- **Phase 3 - Output & CLI:** `render.py`; `cli.py`/`__main__.py`.
- **Phase 4 - Tests:** unit tests; oracle/AC subprocess tests; error-table tests; edge-case tests.

## 8. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| CRLF on Windows stdout | `reconfigure(newline="\n")`; byte-level tests assert no `\r` |
| autocrlf corrupts fixtures | `.gitattributes`; tests write fixtures via `write_bytes` into `tmp_path` |
| Unicode digit / trailing-newline acceptance | `fullmatch` + `[0-9]` |
| `-0.00` output | explicit zero normalization after quantize |
| Context precision silently rounding sums | explicit high-precision context with traps |
| stderr/stdout ordering | build full output, write and flush stdout before warning |
| Tests cannot import package with `cwd=tmp_path` | run subprocess with `cwd` = repo root; pass fixture paths absolute-or-relative accordingly (relative paths for message checks are done with cwd set to `tmp_path` and `PYTHONPATH` = repo root) |
| Python/pytest availability unverified | first implementation task runs `python --version` and `python -m pytest --version` |

## 9. Acceptance Criteria

AC1-AC10 of `contract.md` verbatim, plus: every row of the error table has a test asserting exit code, exact stderr line, and empty stdout; `categorize` has table and JSON tests; `--month` with duplicates verifies the warning counts all inputs; BOM, header-only, 0-byte, CRLF input, multi-line quoted fields, rule priority ties, and non-ASCII descriptions are covered.

## 10. Dependencies on Prior Features

None.

## 11. Delegation to Future Specs

Stdin input, additional output formats, multi-currency, and packaging are out of scope.

---

## Research Decisions and Disagreements

- **Error exit codes.** The CLI researcher recommended a generic exit 1 for runtime/data errors and suggested possibly treating `-` as stdin. **Decision:** `contract.md` governs: exit codes 3/4 for file errors, 1 reserved for unexpected errors only, `-` is an ordinary filename. Alternative recorded and rejected.
- **Row-level rounding.** Web research raised whether to round per row or on aggregates. **Decision:** aggregates are summed unrounded and rounded once (contract money formatting).
- **Regex flags for rule matching.** Research noted `re.IGNORECASE` and `casefold()` differ on some Unicode input. **Decision:** follow contract exactly (`casefold` for `contains`; `re.IGNORECASE` for `regex`).
- **Line numbers on multi-line records.** Research suggested reporting the record start. **Decision:** contract specifies `csv.reader.line_num` after reading the record; follow it.
- **Unverified research items** (blank-row `[]`, field-size limit 131072, NUL handling) are to be verified in a REPL by the implementer; the design above does not depend on them beyond blank-row skipping, which the contract already states.

## Sources

Codebase analyst report (repo audit of `brief.md`, `contract.md`, `.gitignore`); docs.python.org pages for `decimal`, `csv`, `re`, `argparse`, `io`, `codecs`, `subprocess`, `signal`; docs.pytest.org `tmp_path`.

- **Line numbers on multi-line records.** Research suggested reporting the record start. **Decision:** contract specifies `csv.reader.line_num` after reading the record; follow it.
- **Unverified research items** (blank-row `[]`, field-size limit 131072, NUL handling) are to be verified in a REPL by the implementer; the design above does not depend on them beyond blank-row skipping, which the contract already states.

Codebase analyst report (repo audit of `brief.md`, `contract.md`, `.gitignore`); docs.python.org pages for `decimal`, `csv`, `re`, `argparse`, `io`, `codecs`, `subprocess`, `signal`; docs.pytest.org `tmp_path`.

A very long amount that would still overflow the context is reported as the transaction error `invalid amount` (exit 3) rather than a traceback.
3. **Money formatting** exactly per contract: quantize, map zero to `0.00`, else `format(q, "f")`.

4. **Header handling.** Zero-byte file (or BOM-only) → `missing header`. A first record of zero fields (blank first line) is treated as `missing header`. Header names stripped and lowercased; duplicate/missing checks per contract order.

-5. **Reader.** `csv.reader(f)` with defaults per contract. Whole file is read inside the `try` so `UnicodeDecodeError` (not an `OSError`) is mapped to `not valid UTF-8`; `OSError` (including a directory argument, which is `PermissionError` on Windows and `IsADirectoryError` on POSIX) → `cannot read file`. `<line>` is `reader.line_num` after reading the record, per contract. A `csv.Error` (e.g. field larger than the limit) is mapped to `<path>:<line>: expected ... ` is not available, so it is reported as `<path>: cannot read file` (exit 3/4) — an unspecified edge case chosen as the closest contract message.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""validate-task-schema.py
3	
4	Validate that geeky-plan task files (tasks/Tx-*.md) carry the sections the
5	template defines and that geeky-implement relies on. This is the plan->implement
6	boundary gate: run it at the end of geeky-plan and the start of geeky-implement.
7	
8	Required sections (missing => ERROR, file fails):
9	  Task Name, Scope / In scope, Dependencies, Acceptance Criteria,
10	  Tests/Validation Before Next Task, Priority
11	Recommended sections (missing => WARNING):
12	  Context, Module/System, Technical Notes, Definition of Done, Estimate
13	
14	Matching is tolerant: a label counts as present if any line, after stripping
15	leading '#'/'*' markers and whitespace, begins with the label (case-insensitive).
16	
17	Contract (matches the other validators):
18	  argv in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, human summary on stdout.
19	  --json emits a machine-readable object.
20	
21	Usage:
22	  python validate-task-schema.py --path "/abs/path/to/docs/feature-folder"
23	  python validate-task-schema.py --file "/abs/path/to/tasks/T1-foo.md" --json
24	"""
25	
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import argparse
29	import json
30	import re
31	import sys
32	from pathlib import Path
33	
34	REQUIRED = (
35	    ("Task Name", r"Task\s*Name"),
36	    ("In scope", r"In\s*scope"),
37	    ("Dependencies", r"Dependencies"),
38	    ("Acceptance Criteria", r"Acceptance\s*Criteria"),
39	    ("Tests/Validation", r"Tests\s*/\s*Validation"),
40	    ("Priority", r"Priority"),
41	)
42	RECOMMENDED = (
43	    ("Context", r"Context"),
44	    ("Module/System", r"Module\s*/\s*System"),
45	    ("Technical Notes", r"Technical\s*Notes"),
46	    ("Definition of Done", r"Definition\s+of\s+Done"),
47	    ("Estimate", r"Estimate"),
48	)
49	
50	NOTES_RE = re.compile(r"\.notes\.md$", re.IGNORECASE)
51	
52	
53	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
54	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=True)
55	    p.add_argument("--path", dest="path", required=False)
56	    p.add_argument("positional", nargs="?", default=None)
57	    p.add_argument("--file", dest="file", required=False)
58	    p.add_argument("--json", dest="as_json", action="store_true")
59	    return p.parse_args()
60	
61	
62	def label_present(text: str, pattern: str) -> bool:
63	    rx = re.compile(rf"^\s*[#*\s]*{pattern}\b", re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE)
64	    return rx.search(text) is not None
65	
66	
67	def check_file(path: Path) -> dict:
68	    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
69	    missing_required = [name for name, pat in REQUIRED if not label_present(text, pat)]
70	    missing_recommended = [name for name, pat in RECOMMENDED if not label_present(text, pat)]
71	    return {
72	        "file": path.name,
73	        "ok": not missing_required,
74	        "missing_required": missing_required,
75	        "missing_recommended": missing_recommended,
76	    }
77	
78	
79	def collect_task_files(folder: Path) -> list[Path]:
80	    tasks_dir = folder / "tasks"
81	    if not tasks_dir.is_dir():
82	        return []
83	    return sorted(
84	        f for f in tasks_dir.iterdir()
85	        if f.is_file() and f.name.lower().endswith(".md") and not NOTES_RE.search(f.name)
86	        and f.name[:1].upper() == "T"
87	    )
88	
89	
90	def main() -> int:
91	    args = parse_args()
92	
93	    files: list[Path] = []
94	    if args.file:
95	        files = [Path(args.file)]
96	    else:
97	        path_str = args.path or args.positional
98	        if not path_str:
99	            print("USAGE: validate-task-schema.py (--path <folder> | --file <task.md>) [--json]")
100	            return 1
101	        folder = Path(path_str)
102	        if not folder.is_dir():
103	            msg = f"MISSING_FOLDER: {folder}"
104	            print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "errors": [msg]}) if args.as_json else msg)
105	            return 1
106	        files = collect_task_files(folder)
107	
108	    if not files:
109	        msg = "NO_TASK_FILES: nothing to validate (expected tasks/Tx-*.md)"
110	        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "errors": [msg]}) if args.as_json else msg)
111	        return 1
112	
113	    results = []
114	    for f in files:
115	        if not f.is_file():
116	            results.append({"file": str(f), "ok": False,
117	                            "missing_required": ["<file not found>"], "missing_recommended": []})
118	            continue
119	        results.append(check_file(f))
120	
121	    ok = all(r["ok"] for r in results)
122	    failed = sum(1 for r in results if not r["ok"])
123	
124	    if args.as_json:
125	        print(json.dumps({"ok": ok, "results": results}, indent=2))
126	    else:
127	        prefix = "OK" if ok else "INVALID_TASK_SCHEMA"
128	        print(f"{prefix}: {len(results)} task file(s) checked, {failed} failing.")
129	        for r in results:
130	            if r["missing_required"]:
131	                print(f"  {r['file']}:")
132	                for m in r["missing_required"]:
133	                    print(f"    ERROR:   missing required section: {m}")
134	            for m in r["missing_recommended"]:
135	                print(f"    WARNING: {r['file']} missing recommended section: {m}")
136	
137	    return 0 if ok else 1
138	
139	
140	if __name__ == "__main__":
141	    sys.exit(main())

Recommended sections (missing => WARNING):
  Context, Module/System, Technical Notes, Definition of Done, Estimate

Matching is tolerant: a label counts as present if any line, after stripping
leading '#'/'*' markers and whitespace, begins with the label (case-insensitive).

Contract (matches the other validators):
  argv in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, human summary on stdout.
  --json emits a machine-readable object.

Usage:
  python validate-task-schema.py --path "/abs/path/to/docs/feature-folder"
  python validate-task-schema.py --file "/abs/path/to/tasks/T1-foo.md" --json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REQUIRED = (
    ("Task Name", r"Task\s*Name"),
    ("In scope", r"In\s*scope"),
    ("Dependencies", r"Dependencies"),
    ("Acceptance Criteria", r"Acceptance\s*Criteria"),
    ("Tests/Validation", r"Tests\s*/\s*Validation"),
    ("Priority", r"Priority"),
)
RECOMMENDED = (
    ("Context", r"Context"),
    ("Module/System", r"Module\s*/\s*System"),
    ("Technical Notes", r"Technical\s*Notes"),
    ("Definition of Done", r"Definition\s+of\s+Done"),
    ("Estimate", r"Estimate"),
)

NOTES_RE = re.compile(r"\.notes\.md$", re.IGNORECASE)


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=True)
    p.add_argument("--path", dest="path", required=False)
    p.add_argument("positional", nargs="?", default=None)
    p.add_argument("--file", dest="file", required=False)
    p.add_argument("--json", dest="as_json", action="store_true")
    return p.parse_args()


def label_present(text: str, pattern: str) -> bool:
    rx = re.compile(rf"^\s*[#*\s]*{pattern}\b", re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE)
    return rx.search(text) is not None


def check_file(path: Path) -> dict:
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    missing_required = [name for name, pat in REQUIRED if not label_present(text, pat)]
    missing_recommended = [name for name, pat in RECOMMENDED if not label_present(text, pat)]
    return {
        "file": path.name,
        "ok": not missing_required,
        "missing_required": missing_required,
        "missing_recommended": missing_recommended,
    }


def collect_task_files(folder: Path) -> list[Path]:
    tasks_dir = folder / "tasks"
    if not tasks_dir.is_dir():
        return []
    return sorted(
        f for f in tasks_dir.iterdir()
        if f.is_file() and f.name.lower().endswith(".md") and not NOTES_RE.search(f.name)
        and f.name[:1].upper() == "T"
    )


def main() -> int:
    args = parse_args()

    files: list[Path] = []
    if args.file:
        files = [Path(args.file)]
    else:
        path_str = args.path or args.positional
        if not path_str:
            print("USAGE: validate-task-schema.py (--path <folder> | --file <task.md>) [--json]")
            return 1
        folder = Path(path_str)
        if not folder.is_dir():
            msg = f"MISSING_FOLDER: {folder}"
            print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "errors": [msg]}) if args.as_json else msg)
            return 1
        files = collect_task_files(folder)

    if not files:
        msg = "NO_TASK_FILES: nothing to validate (expected tasks/Tx-*.md)"
        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "errors": [msg]}) if args.as_json else msg)
        return 1

    results = []
    for f in files:
        if not f.is_file():
            results.append({"file": str(f), "ok": False,
                            "missing_required": ["<file not found>"], "missing_recommended": []})
            continue
        results.append(check_file(f))

    ok = all(r["ok"] for r in results)
    failed = sum(1 for r in results if not r["ok"])

    if args.as_json:
        print(json.dumps({"ok": ok, "results": results}, indent=2))
    else:
        prefix = "OK" if ok else "INVALID_TASK_SCHEMA"
        print(f"{prefix}: {len(results)} task file(s) checked, {failed} failing.")
        for r in results:
            if r["missing_required"]:
                print(f"  {r['file']}:")
                for m in r["missing_required"]:
                    print(f"    ERROR:   missing required section: {m}")
            for m in r["missing_recommended"]:
                print(f"    WARNING: {r['file']} missing recommended section: {m}")

    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

3

5	Replaces LLM self-report ("I updated the board") with a fail-stop check.
6

8	  ERROR   - a task file in tasks/ is not placed in any lane (untracked)

13	
14	Recognised lanes (case-insensitive, any heading depth): Backlog, Ready,
15	In Progress, In Review, Blocked, Done. A heading containing "validation" is
16	treated as the release-gate checklist, not a task lane.

18	Contract (matches the other validators):
19	  argv in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, human summary on stdout.

34

36	KNOWN_LANES = ("Backlog", "Ready", "In Progress", "In Review", "Blocked", "Done")

40	TASK_FILE_RE = re.compile(r"^T\d+", re.IGNORECASE)

45	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=True)
46	    p.add_argument("--path", dest="path", required=False)
47	    p.add_argument("positional", nargs="?", default=None)
48	    p.add_argument("--wip", type=int, default=3, help="In Progress WIP cap (default 3)")
49	    p.add_argument("--json", dest="as_json", action="store_true")
50	    return p.parse_args()
51

53	def lane_for_heading(heading: str) -> str | None:
54	    """Return the canonical lane name for a heading, or None."""
55	    norm = heading.strip().lower()
56	    if "validation" in norm:
57	        return None
58	    for lane in KNOWN_LANES:
59	        if norm == lane.lower() or norm.startswith(lane.lower()):
60	            return lane
61	    return None

65	    ids: set[str] = set()
66	    if not tasks_dir.is_dir():
67	        return ids

69	        if not f.is_file():
70	            continue
71	        if NOTES_RE.search(f.name) or not f.name.lower().endswith(".md"):
72	            continue
73	        m = TASK_FILE_RE.match(f.name)
74	        if m:
75	            ids.add(m.group(0).upper())
76	    return ids

80	    """Map canonical lane -> set of task ids referenced under it, and the set of

82	    placements: dict[str, set[str]] = {lane: set() for lane in KNOWN_LANES}
83	    present: set[str] = set()

104	    if not kanban.is_file():

108	            "warnings": [],
109	            "lane_counts": {},

116	    )

123

125	    for tid in sorted(file_ids):
126	        if tid not in id_lanes:
127	            errors.append(f"{tid} has a task file but is not placed in any kanban lane")
128	
129	    # Ambiguous: placed in more than one lane.
130	    for tid, lanes in sorted(id_lanes.items()):
131	        if len(lanes) > 1:
132	            errors.append(f"{tid} appears in multiple lanes: {', '.join(sorted(lanes))}")
133	
134	    # Dangling: referenced in kanban but no task file.
135	    for tid in sorted(id_lanes):
136	        if file_ids and tid not in file_ids:
137	            warnings.append(f"{tid} is referenced in the kanban but has no tasks/{tid}-*.md file")
138

141	        if lane not in present_lanes:

147	        warnings.append(f"In Progress has {in_progress} tasks (WIP cap {wip_cap})")
148	
149	    lane_counts = {lane: len(ids) for lane, ids in placements.items()}
150	    tracked = len({tid for ids in placements.values() for tid in ids})
151	
152	    ok = not errors
153	    summary = (
154	        f"{'OK' if ok else 'INVALID_KANBAN'}: {tracked} task(s) tracked, "
155	        f"{len(file_ids)} task file(s). "
156	        + ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in lane_counts.items())
157	    )
158	    return {
159	        "ok": ok,
160	        "errors": errors,
161	        "warnings": warnings,
162	        "lane_counts": lane_counts,
163	        "summary": summary,
164	    }
165	
166	
167	def main() -> int:
168	    args = parse_args()
169	    path_str = args.path or args.positional
170	    if not path_str:
171	        print("USAGE: validate-kanban.py --path <folder> [--wip N] [--json]")
172	        return 1
173	
174	    folder = Path(path_str)
175	    if not folder.is_dir():
176	        msg = f"MISSING_FOLDER: {folder}"
177	        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "errors": [msg]}) if args.as_json else msg)
178	        return 1
179	
180	    report = build_report(folder, args.wip)
181	
182	    if args.as_json:
183	        print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
184	    else:
185	        print(report["summary"])
186	        for e in report["errors"]:
187	            print(f"  ERROR:   {e}")
188	        for w in report["warnings"]:
189	            print(f"  WARNING: {w}")
190	
191	    return 0 if report["ok"] else 1
192	
193	
194	if __name__ == "__main__":
195	    sys.exit(main())
